en.title: Maximum Meetings While Keeping the Index Positive
en.description:
The effectiveness index starts at 0. Each meeting increases or decreases the index by effectiveness[i]. You may choose and reorder meetings freely; after each scheduled meeting ends, the index must be strictly greater than 0. Find the maximum number of meetings that can be scheduled.

This problem uses the CSWork standard input/output format. Akuna #20 and Goldman Sachs #22 have the same statement and ranges; since the original Akuna page has no examples, the illustrative example below is taken from #22 to make clear that meetings can be reordered.
en.input: The first line contains n (1..100000), and the second line contains n integers effectiveness[i] (−10^9..10^9).
en.output: Output the maximum number of meetings that can be attended in a row such that the index is strictly positive after each one ends.
en.explanation: The example is taken from Goldman Sachs #22, which has the same statement; its schedule order shows that meetings can be reordered.
hints: Sort by effectiveness from largest to smallest and add meetings one by one; keep a meeting as long as the new running index is still strictly greater than 0, otherwise no later value can rescue that prefix.
